tools.name: open_board
tools.description: Open a new, empty board and get its link. Give the link to the user: they watch your work there and download it.

tools.name: read_board
tools.description: Read a board: its kind and current content (the Markdown or HTML text, or the doodle's elements with their ids, roles, boxes and styles).

tools.name: write_board
tools.description: Replace everything on an HTML or Markdown board. HTML: one complete document with inline CSS and JS. Markdown: GitHub-flavored. For a doodle, use `draw` instead.

tools.name: edit_text
tools.description:
Change part of an HTML or Markdown board without resending all of it.
Ops (applied in order, all or nothing):
- {"op": "write", "text": "..."} (replace everything)
- {"op": "append", "text": "..."}
- {"op": "replace", "find": "...", "replace": "..."} (find must occur exactly once)

tools.name: draw
tools.description:
Draw on a doodle board. The user sees each call appear live in the editor.
## Doodle ops

A doodle is a board (default 1280 x 720 px, origin top-left, y grows down). Send ops as
`{"ops": [...]}`; they apply in order, all or nothing. The answer lists the ids each op
created, in order. Address element

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "draw" is 4280 chars, far longer than this server's median (161). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_board, draw · Private data: write_board · Public sink: draw · Destructive: draw.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_board, draw · Private data: write_board · Public sink: draw · Destructive: draw

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
